word_for_word: किंच दुःखेष्विति
and further, with ‘in sufferings’
दुःखेषु प्राप्तेष्वप्यनुद्विग्नमक्षुभितं मनो यस्य सः
one whose mind remains unagitated, unshaken, even when sufferings arise
सुखेषु विगता स्पृहा यस्य सः
one whose longing has departed in pleasures
तत्र हेतुः वीतापगता रागभयक्रोधा यस्मात्
the reason is that attachment, fear, and anger have departed from him
तत्र रागः प्रीतिः
there ‘attachment’ means affection
स मुनिः स्थितधीः स्थितप्रज्ञ इत्युच्यते
that sage is called one of steady understanding, steady wisdom
कथं भाषेतेत्यस्योत्तरमाह य इति
he answers ‘how does he speak?’ with ‘he who’
यः सर्वत्र पुत्रादिष्वप्यनभिस्नेहः स्नेहशून्यः
one who is without special attachment everywhere, even toward sons and the like, devoid of attachment
अतएव बाधितानुवृत्त्या तत्तच्छुभमनुकूलं प्राप्य नाभिनन्दति न प्रशंसति
therefore, though conventional responses continue, on obtaining something favorable and auspicious he neither rejoices in nor praises it
अशुभं प्रतिकूलं प्राप्य न द्वेष्टि न निन्दति
on obtaining something unfavorable and inauspicious he neither hates nor condemns it
किंतु केवलमुदासीन एव भाषते
rather, he speaks remaining merely indifferent
तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठितेत्यर्थः
his wisdom is established; this is the meaning
किंच यदेति
and further, with ‘when’
यदा चायं योगी इन्द्रियार्थेभ्यः सकाशादिन्द्रियाणि संहरते प्रत्याहरति
when this yogin withdraws, draws back, the senses from their objects
अनायासेन संहारे दृष्टान्तः
an example is given for effortless withdrawal
अङ्गानि करचरणादीनि कूर्मो यथा स्वभावेनैवाकर्षति तद्वत्
just as a tortoise naturally draws in its limbs, hands, feet, and the like, so does he
ननु नेन्द्रियाणां विषयेष्वप्रवृत्तिः स्थितप्रज्ञस्य लक्षणं भवितुमर्हति
objection: non-engagement of the senses in objects cannot be a characteristic of one of steady wisdom
जडानामातुराणामुपवासपराणां च विषयेष्वप्रवृत्तेरविशेषात्तत्राह विषया इति
because insentient persons, the sick, and those devoted to fasting likewise do not engage in objects; to this he says ‘objects’
इन्द्रियैर्विषयाणामाहरणं ग्रहणमाहारः
‘āhāra’ is the taking, grasping, of objects by the senses
निराहारस्येन्द्रियैर्विषयग्रहणमकुर्वतो देहिनो देहाभिमानिनोऽज्ञस्य विषया विनिवर्तन्ते
for an ignorant embodied person identifying with the body who is ‘without food,’ not grasping objects with the senses, the objects withdraw
तदनुभवो निवर्तत इत्यर्थः
experience of them ceases; this is the meaning
किंतु रसो रागोऽभिलाषस्तद्वर्जम् अभिलाषस्तु न निवर्तत इत्यर्थः
but not the taste, attachment, longing; longing does not cease
रसोऽपि रागोऽपि परं परमात्मानं दृष्ट्वाऽस्य स्थितप्रज्ञस्य स्वतो निवर्तते नश्यतीत्यर्थः
even the taste, the attachment, spontaneously ceases and is destroyed in one of steady wisdom after seeing the Supreme, the Supreme Self
यद्वा निराहारस्योपवासपरस्य विषयाः प्रायशो विनिवर्तन्ते क्षुधासंतप्तस्य शब्दस्पर्शाद्यपेक्षाभावात्
or: for one fasting, objects mostly withdraw because a person tormented by hunger has no concern for sound, touch, and the like
परंतु रसवर्जम् रसापेक्षा तु न निवर्तत इत्यर्थः
but not taste; expectation of taste does not cease; this is the meaning
शेषं समानम्
the rest is the same
इन्द्रियसंयमं विना तु स्थितप्रज्ञता न संभवति
without restraint of the senses, steady wisdom is not possible
अतः साधकावस्थायां तत्र महान्प्रयत्नः कर्तव्य इत्याह यततो ह्यपीति द्वाभ्याम्
therefore in the stage of practice great effort must be made there; he states this in two verses beginning ‘even of one striving’
यततो मोक्षे प्रयतमानस्यापि विपश्चितो विवेकिनोऽपि मन इन्द्रियाणि प्रसभं बलाद्धरन्ति
the senses forcibly carry away the mind even of a discerning person striving for liberation
यतः प्रमाथीनि प्रमथनशीलानि प्रक्षोभकाणि
because they are turbulent, disposed to churn up, agitating
यस्मादेवं तस्मात् तानीति
because this is so, therefore with ‘those’
युक्तो योगी तानीन्द्रियाणि संयम्य मत्परः सन्नासीत
the disciplined yogin should sit restraining those senses and taking Me as supreme
यस्य वशे वशवर्तीनि
the senses are under the control of one whose they are
एतेन कथमासीतेति प्रश्नस्य वशीकृतेन्द्रियः सन्नासीतेत्युत्तरमुक्तं भवति
by this the question ‘how does he sit?’ is answered: he sits having brought the senses under control
बाह्येन्द्रियसंयमाभावे दोषमुक्त्वा मनःसंयमाभावे दोषमाह ध्यायत इति द्वाभ्याम्
having stated the fault in absence of restraint of the outer senses, he states the fault in absence of restraint of the mind in two verses beginning ‘while contemplating’
गुणबुद्ध्या विषयान्ध्यायतः पुरुषस्य तेषु सङ्ग आसक्तिर्भवति
for a person contemplating sense objects with the notion that they possess desirable qualities, attachment to them arises
आसक्त्या तु तेष्वधिकः कामो भवति
from attachment greater desire for them arises
कामाच्च केनचित्प्रतिहतात्क्रोधो भवति
and when desire is obstructed by someone, anger arises
किंच क्रोधादिति
and further, with ‘from anger’
क्रोधात्संमोहः कार्याकार्यविवेकाभावः
from anger comes delusion, absence of discrimination between what should and should not be done
ततः शास्त्राचार्योपदिष्टार्थस्मृतेर्विभ्रमो विचलनम्
from that comes confusion, displacement, of memory of the meanings taught by scripture and teacher
ततो बुद्धेश्चेतनाया विनाशो वृक्षादिष्विवाभिभवः
from that comes destruction, overpowering, of intelligence, consciousness, as in trees and the like
ततः प्रणश्यति मृततुल्यो भवति
thereafter one perishes, becoming like the dead
नन्विन्द्रियाणां विषयप्रवणस्वभावानां विरोद्धुमशक्यत्वादयं दोषो दुष्परिहर इति स्थितप्रज्ञत्वं कथं स्यादित्याशङ्क्याह रागेति द्वाभ्याम्

objection: since senses naturally incline toward objects and cannot be opposed, this fault is difficult to avoid; how can steady wisdom arise? anticipating this he answers in two verses beginning ‘attachment’
रागद्वेषरहितैर्विगतदर्पैरिन्द्रियैर्विषयांश्चरन्भुञ्जानोऽपि प्रसादं शान्तिं प्राप्नोति
even while moving among and enjoying objects through senses free from attachment and aversion, with pride gone, one attains clarity, peace
रागद्वेषराहित्यमेवाह आत्मनो मनसो वश्यैर्विधेयो वशवर्ती आत्मा मनो यस्येति
he explains freedom from attachment and aversion: the senses are controlled by the self, the mind; one whose mind is obedient and under control
अनेनैव कथं व्रजेत भुञ्जीतेत्यस्य चतुर्थप्रश्नस्य स्वाधीनैरिन्द्रियैर्विषयानधिगच्छतीत्युत्तरमुक्तं भवति
by this the fourth question, how he moves and enjoys, is answered: he approaches objects with senses under his own control
प्रसादे सति किं स्यादित्यत्राह प्रसाद इति
what happens when clarity is present? he says ‘in clarity’
प्रसादे सति सर्वदुःखनाशस्ततश्च प्रसन्नचेतसो बुद्धिः प्रतिष्ठिता भवतीत्यर्थः
when clarity is present, all suffering is destroyed; then the understanding of one whose mind is serene becomes established; this is the meaning
इन्द्रियनिग्रहस्य स्थितप्रज्ञतासाधनत्वं व्यतिरेकमुखेनोपपादयति नास्तीति
he establishes, by the negative method, that restraint of the senses is a means to steady wisdom with ‘there is not’
अयुक्तस्यावशीकृतेन्द्रियस्य नास्ति बुद्धिः शास्त्राचार्योपदेशाभ्यामात्मविषया बुद्धिः प्रज्ञैव नोत्पद्यते
for the undisciplined person whose senses are uncontrolled, understanding concerning the Self, wisdom born from instruction by scripture and teacher, does not arise
कुतस्तस्य प्रतिष्ठा वार्ता वा कुत इत्यत आह न चायुक्तस्य भावना ध्यानम्
how then could establishment of that understanding even be discussed? to this he says: for the undisciplined there is no contemplation, meditation
भावनया हि बुद्धेरात्मनि प्रतिष्ठा भवति सा चायुक्तस्य यतो नास्ति
for through contemplation understanding becomes established in the Self, and such contemplation is absent for the undisciplined
न चाभावयत आत्मध्यानमकुर्वतः शान्तिरात्मनि चित्तोपरतिः
nor does one who does not contemplate, who does not meditate on the Self, have peace, cessation of mind in the Self
अशान्तस्य कुतः सुखं मोक्षानन्द इत्यर्थः
how can one without peace have happiness, the bliss of liberation? this is the meaning
